output.brief:
The evidence doesn't show that the three-person night rota caused the rise in falls, and it doesn't rule it out. Q3 falls (3.7 per 1,000 bed days at both homes) are inside each home's historical range. Q2 was unusually low, near the bottom of each home's range. The app also went live on 1 July, and the Q2 handover-note check found three clear unreported falls and three ambiguous entries in the six weeks that could be checked. That points to Q2 being under-recorded and the app capturing more, especially no-harm and "found on floor" falls. Harm-level falls rose only slightly. Frailer admissions and new GP prescribing are untested. Nobody can say whether call bells are slower, because no pre-June timings exist.

I'd keep the pilot under its existing pause criteria. Re-present falls as rates, with the recording change marked. Start manual sampling of night call-bell response times now. Review the rollout in late January with Q4 data. Reversing the rota now is premature. Warnings to night seniors, or reverting the app to paper, would be harmful. Confidence is moderate. A real rota effect of around 40% could still be hidden, so the January review matters.
